note: A Sonnet agent was sent to adversarially audit the two §6.92 fixes just shipped on this branch (finding 3, the add_pair reason retry; finding 1, the bundle matcher label). Finding 3 came back sound — all 15 add_pair parameters forwarded, the test a real gate, the race simulation hitting the genuine IntegrityError path. Finding 1's portable.py MECHANISM came back sound too — label outside the digest, rows keyed on the bundle's own source_norm, tests real gates. But the audit caught that the mechanism was only wired correctly on /api/import: the UI 'Export bundle' button and both CLI subcommands silently reverted to the process default, reintroducing the exact mislabel finding 1 exists to close, on the export side. These are the decisions that fixing the wiring produced. The lesson is filed separately in the note below because it is the part worth keeping.

decisions.question: The UI 'Export bundle' button sends no domain tags. What matcher label should its whole-store export carry?
decisions.commitment: The surface's own app.matcher. A domain-SCOPED request still routes through _domain_matcher (app.matcher for the App's domain, defer for another); only the unscoped whole-store export takes app.matcher directly.
decisions.why: _domain_matcher exists to stop the surface lending its matcher to a request about ANOTHER domain — the §6.40 regression, where an alias rejection got keyed by the wrong domain's matcher. That guard is right for keying and serving, and it was reused for the export label unchanged. But an unscoped export is not a request about another domain; it is this surface exporting the rows it manages, and the button that triggers it (ui_page.py, a bare <a href=/api/bundle>) sends no tags at all. So _domain_matcher('','') returned None, the label fell to the process default, and a NumericMatcher surface exported a bundle stamped StringMatcher — which on import into a StringMatcher destination reports matcher_mismatch:False while the rows land dead. app.matcher is the honest label for the unscoped case: it is what keyed the rows this surface is responsible for. The residual, stated rather than hidden: a store holding a SECOND domain keyed differently cannot be captured by one label, because the envelope field is singular and the export is whole-store. The label is advisory (decision 0073), so a per-domain label set is a separate, larger change left open, not a blocker on closing the common case.

decisions.question: The CLI export/import had no --matcher flag, so they always labelled with the process global. Add one, or accept the default?
decisions.commitment: Add --matcher to both, resolved through answer.load_matcher exactly as ask/match/calibrate already do; default 'string' resolves to None, so the unflagged behaviour is unchanged.
decisions.why: The store records no per-domain matcher, so a `nestor export` process cannot recover what keyed its rows — and the common way a custom-matcher store comes to exist is `nestor ui --matcher acme:M` or `nestor serve --matcher acme:M`, a DIFFERENT, long-lived process, after which a separate short-lived `nestor export` starts with its global reset to the StringMatcher default. So the process global is not 'the honest answer' the first version claimed; it is a guess that is wrong precisely when a custom matcher is in play. The operator is the one party who knows which matcher sealed the rows, so the flag is how they assert it — the same shape load_matcher already serves for the surfaces that key rather than transport. Defaulting to None (via load_matcher('string')) keeps every existing invocation byte-for-byte, so this is additive.

decisions.question: What did the audit change about how this kind of fix is tested?
decisions.commitment: Test the surface, not only the seam. The four original finding-1 tests called export_bundle/import_bundle directly with an explicit matcher= kwarg, so they gated the mechanism and never the wiring that feeds it — the two paths that were broken had no test at all.
decisions.why: This is decision 0071's own lesson arriving one layer out: there, an API-layer test certified a refusal while the only client sent the field that made the refusal a regression, and the rule was 'test the client, not only the endpoint'. Here the seam-level tests all passed on the broken revision because they bypassed the wiring entirely — ui._bundle and the CLI parsers were never exercised with a non-default matcher. The new tests drive ui._bundle with an empty query (the actual button) and run cli.main export/import with --matcher through a subprocess-shaped path, and each fails on the pre-wiring revision (the CLI with 'unrecognized arguments: --matcher', the UI with the process-default label). A guard test also pins that a domain-scoped export to a FOREIGN domain still defers, so the §6.40 guard the fix routes around is not quietly lost. The general form: when a fix is a mechanism plus the wiring that supplies its input, a test that constructs the input by hand proves the mechanism and certifies nothing about the wiring — and the wiring is where this class of defect lives.
